{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-08",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["PATCH /users/{id} endpoint", "User update handler", "User record mapper"],
    "dataStores": ["User record store"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Authenticated user to user API"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "User makes themselves an admin by adding a role field to the update request",
      "scenario": "Any logged-in user calls PATCH /users/{id} on their own account with an extra field such as {\"role\":\"admin\"}. Because the handler copies every field in the JSON body onto the user record, the role is overwritten and the attacker gains administrative privileges across the API with a single request and no special tooling.",
      "component": "PATCH /users/{id} update handler",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "copies every field onto the user record, including fields like role and accountStatus" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.3", "V13.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915", "CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "A normal user can add \"role\": \"admin\" to a profile update and become an administrator.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind only an explicit allow-list of updatable profile fields",
        "given": "an authenticated user sends PATCH /users/{id}",
        "when": "the body contains fields outside the allow-list such as role or accountStatus",
        "then": "those fields are ignored or the request is rejected, and the stored role and accountStatus are unchanged"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Attacker reactivates or unlocks an account by setting accountStatus",
      "scenario": "A user whose account was suspended, locked or pending verification sends PATCH /users/{id} with {\"accountStatus\":\"active\"}. The handler copies the field straight onto the record, undoing a moderation or security decision such as a lockout after fraud or failed logins, and restoring access the business intended to remove.",
      "component": "User record mapper",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "copies every field onto the user record, including fields like role and accountStatus" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915", "CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "A suspended user could switch their own account back to active by adding one field to a profile update.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Account status changes only via the moderation path",
        "given": "a user update request includes accountStatus",
        "when": "the caller is not an authorised administrator using the moderation endpoint",
        "then": "the value is discarded and the existing account status is preserved"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Any user can update another user's record because {id} is taken from the URL",
      "scenario": "The design states users call PATCH /users/{id} to update their display name, but describes no check that {id} is the caller. An attacker enumerates or guesses another user's id and sends a PATCH, changing that person's profile and, combined with the mass assignment flaw, their role or account status, taking over other accounts.",
      "component": "PATCH /users/{id} endpoint authorisation",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "PATCH /users/{id} accepts a JSON body" },
        { "quote": "Users call it to update their display name." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1", "V4.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639", "CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing described stops a user putting someone else's id in the URL and editing their account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce ownership on user update",
        "given": "an authenticated caller sends PATCH /users/{id}",
        "when": "{id} does not belong to the caller and the caller is not an administrator",
        "then": "the API returns a 403 and makes no change to the target record"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Identity fields such as email or username can be overwritten to hijack a login or reset",
      "scenario": "Because every field in the body is copied onto the user record, an attacker can send fields that identify the account, for example an email address or username belonging to a colleague, or flags such as emailVerified. They then use password reset or email-based login against the changed identity to receive the victim's messages or access.",
      "component": "User record mapper",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "copies every field onto the user record" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because every submitted field is saved, someone could overwrite the email on an account and take over logins tied to it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Identity and verification fields are immutable through profile update",
        "given": "a PATCH /users/{id} body containing email, username or verification flags",
        "when": "the request is processed",
        "then": "those fields are rejected and any email change goes through a separate verified change-of-email flow"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Internal and relational fields can be forged by sending unknown keys",
      "scenario": "The copy-everything mapper also accepts fields the API authors never meant to expose, such as internal ids, tenant or organisation references, timestamps or balance-like counters. An attacker experiments with field names until one sticks, then moves their user into another tenant's scope or rewrites audit-relevant timestamps, corrupting data integrity.",
      "component": "User update handler",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts a JSON body and copies every field onto the user record" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.3", "V2.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915", "CWE-20"],
      "plainLanguage": "Unknown field names are saved too, so attackers can guess internal fields and change things the API never meant to expose.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reject unknown fields on user update",
        "given": "a PATCH /users/{id} request body",
        "when": "it contains any key not in the documented updatable schema",
        "then": "the request is rejected with 400 and nothing is written"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Privilege changes made through the profile endpoint leave no attributable trail",
      "scenario": "Role and accountStatus changes arrive as ordinary display-name updates on PATCH /users/{id}, so no privilege-change event is recorded and nobody is notified. An attacker who escalates can act as an administrator while investigators see only a routine profile edit, and the escalation cannot be attributed or reliably detected afterwards.",
      "component": "User update handler",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "including fields like role and accountStatus" },
        { "quote": "Users call it to update their display name." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "A role change hidden inside a normal profile update would not be recorded as a role change, so no one would notice.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Record and alert on privilege or status changes",
        "given": "a user's role or accountStatus changes",
        "when": "the change is persisted by any code path",
        "then": "a distinct security event with actor, target, old and new value is written and the affected user is notified"
      }
    }
  ]
}
